To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the h-BN passivation layer enhances the built-in electric potential and hence the open-circuit voltage of the graphene/h-BN/silicon heterojunction photovoltaic cell.
the graphene-on-Si solar cell performance is improved by introducing h-BN as a tunneling layer.
we have developed a new class of heterojunction solar devices with high performance and stability by interfacing graphene with hexagonal boron-nitride (h-Bn) on a silicon substrate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, synthesis, and characterization of graphene/h-Bn/Si heterojuncton solar cells.
the development of new 2-D/2-D/3-D nanoarchitectures and their integration with conventional semiconductor substrates.
the design, fabrication, characterization and modeling of novel graphene-based optoelectronic devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the graphene/h-BN interface is a viable platform to achieve high performance and stable graphene/Si heterojucton solar cells.
the temperature dependent photoluminescence and photovoltaic characteristics are examined on graphene/h-BN/silicon heterojunction solar-cell architecture.
the graphene/h-BN/ lightly-doped Si heterojunction solar-cell exhibits a 3.5-fold increase in power-conversion efficiency (PCE) and ~4% VOC degradation per 10 K increase of temperature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated the use of graphene/h-Bn/Si heterostructure as a photovoltaic device.
graphene/h-BN heterostructure is an excellent platform for the fabrication of high performance, mechanically-robust and durable optoelectric devices.
we have successfully developed an efficient graphene/h-BN/silicon heterojunction photovoltaic cell by employing a bottom-up approach.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the graphene/h-BN interface is a promising candidate for high performance graphene/Si heterojunctio solar cell applications.
the graphene/h-BN interface can provide a high barrier height, which can be utilized in future optoelectronic devices such as photodetectors and solar cells.
the h-BN layer can be utilized as an electron-blocking interlayer in graphene-based optoelectronic devices to enhance the built-in potential and hence the device performance.
